thread:
matt: heads up — overnight loadtest showed a sharp p99 tail spike on the conv-rewrite workload. looks like kernel selector flips + kvcache churn coincided with a burst.
anya: saw those graphs. microbatch was 16 for the test; GPUs climbed to ~96% then admission kept letting requests through. p99 went from ~220ms -> ~1.2s. p95 mostly stable. :grimacing:
cheng: I pulled the perf traces. kernel_switch_count doubled in the spike window; we also see a lot of host->device transfers from prefetch attempts that later got evicted. kvcache churn + large microbatches = bad combo.
raul: that matches my intuition. when util is high the expensive kernel path (full-attn fused kernels) is chosen more often; combined with aggressive prefetch we saturate PCIe and cause tail latency.
matt: high-level options: 1) throttle prefetch parallelism under high gpu_util, 2) force the 'fast-path' kernel for shorter sequences even if slower per-token in steady-state, 3) reduce microbatch cap for KV-heavy requests, 4) tighten admission when p99 climbs.
anya: quick numbers: if we drop microbatch from 16->8 we lose ~7-9% throughput on synthetic steady load but p99 improves ~45% in the KV-heavy test. that's a pretty clear latency win for user-facing SLOs.
cheng: proposed canary config to try on dcs-3 (10% traffic):
```
runtime.admission.max_inflight = 64
runtime.prefetch.parallelism = 2
runtime.kernelselect.force_fast_path_for_seq_lt = 128
runtime.microbatch.max_size = 8
```
That forces lighter prefetch and limits microbatching for conversational sequences.
raul: also add an adaptive demotion: if gpu_util > 85% && p99 > 400ms then reduce prefetch.parallelism by 1 and clamp microbatch to 4 for 30s. simple hysteresis to avoid oscillation.
perf-bot: canary rolled to dcs-3 at 03:12 UTC. initial 10m: p95 flat, p99 decreased ~35%, gpu_util down ~6%. will report 1h metrics.
anya: looking at canary logs — fewer kvcache evictions but a subset of long-seq requests still hit the expensive kernel path and spike. maybe we should demote prefetch for models with large KV footprint first (demote big seq models earlier).
matt: good call. priority demotion list: [m-13b-chat, m-7b-long] (scoped by seq length + kv size). we can target that in kernel selection rules.
cheng: TL;DR: microbatch cap 8 + prefetched parallelism 2 + selective fast-path selection gives p99 win with modest throughput hit. next steps: run 4h canary, gather p95/p99, gpu_util, kvcache_evictions, kernel_switch_count.
raul: rollout plan: 10% -> 30% -> 100% if p99 improves and no regression in overall throughput beyond 12%. add alert: alert if p99 increases while gpu_util decreases (indicative of scheduling/kernelflip issues).
matt: I'll open an RFC with the canary dashboards and perf traces. scheduling a 30min sync at 14:00 to decide on 4h canary, will attach commands to pull metrics.
cheng: quick helper — to fetch canary metrics:
```
# check canary metrics
curl -s 'https://console.api/metrics?service=runtime&canary=dcs-3&window=10m' | jq '.p95, .p99, .gpu_util, .kvcache_evictions'
```
anya: thanks. tiny note: we should expect throughput to drop on small-batch workloads; communicate to customers on the canary group so they can opt-in/out if needed. :memo:
matt: agreed. I'll draft the customer note and RFC. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
